headline: Abra Suspends In-Person Classes; Atok, Benguet Follows Amid Habagat Risks
seoTitle: Abra, Atok Suspend In-Person Classes on August 24 | FMB News
seoDescription: Abra suspended face-to-face classes province-wide while Atok, Benguet halted in-person classes as Habagat conditions kept landslide and travel risks elevated on August 24.
deck: Local governments moved students to alternative learning arrangements as monsoon conditions continued to threaten saturated mountain roads and communities.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Abra suspended face-to-face classes in public and private schools for Monday, August 24, with affected learners shifting to alternative learning modalities. Government offices in the province also moved to alternative arrangements, according to current suspension advisories.
In Benguet, Atok suspended in-person classes from preschool through senior high school. Current independently retrievable advisories support the Atok suspension, not a province-wide Benguet shutdown.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The approved FMB News brief described broader Northern Luzon precautionary measures as the Southwest Monsoon continued to affect saturated upland areas. FMB News narrowed the published scope to the locations that could be independently corroborated as of early Monday.
Several other LGUs also announced localized suspensions for August 24, but the exact coverage varies by municipality and school level.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Highland roads and communities are especially exposed to rockfall, landslide and visibility hazards after repeated rainfall. Localized suspensions allow schools and public offices to reduce travel while keeping learning continuity measures in place.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: Parents, students and government employees should follow their provincial, municipal and school channels for any expansion, extension or lifting of the August 24 suspension orders.
